steps.label: A1
steps.statement: \text{Domain } 0<x<L,\ t>0;\quad k,\ \rho,\ c_p \text{ constant},\ k>0,\ \rho>0,\ c_p>0,\ L>0;\quad T_{ref} \text{ constant in } x \text{ and } t;\ \text{1D rod with no lateral heat exchange}
steps.source: problem.md line 8; spec_problem.md lines 11-13, 27-28, 71 (caloric law e = rho c_p (T - T_ref) with rho, c_p constant; T_ref is the fixed zero of the energy scale). The T_ref clause was added at M3 try 3 (G:Derivation send-back note, decisions.json 2026-11-16T18:28:21-08:00).
steps.if_wrong: If k depended on T, conduction would become \partial_x(k(T)\partial_x T), adding k'(T)(\partial_x T)^2 to S15 (relative size ~ beta*DeltaT_max = beta*Q/8). Lateral losses would add a sink -(hP/A)(T-T_amb). Both are out of scope by the brief (problem.md line 21). If T_ref depended on t, S13 would gain the term -\rho c_p\,dT_{ref}/dt (scratch/m3_try3.py output line 1): a fictitious uniform sink with no physical meaning, since a reference of the energy scale cannot change the physics. If T_ref depended on x, \partial_t e would be unchanged, so S13 would still hold.

steps.label: A2
steps.statement: \frac{d}{dt}\int_a^b e\,dx = j(a,t) - j(b,t) + \int_a^b q\,dx \quad \text{for every } 0\le a<b\le L
steps.source: Conservation of energy for a rigid, motionless segment; spec_problem.md Mechanisms table (lines 24-29) puts only conduction, source and storage in.
steps.if_wrong: Any other energy channel (advection, radiation, mechanical work, latent heat) would add a term to the right side and to S12. All are out of scope (problem.md line 21).

steps.label: A3
steps.if_wrong: With c_p(T), storage becomes \rho c_p(T)\partial_t T (still valid pointwise) but S16-S25 gain a T-dependent coefficient; with phase change a latent term appears.

steps.label: A4
steps.if_wrong: A non-Fourier flux (e.g. Cattaneo relaxation) would make S15 hyperbolic; irrelevant at the continuum scales of the brief.

steps.label: A5
steps.statement: q \in \mathbb{R} \text{ constant in } x \text{ and } t
steps.source: problem.md line 8; decisions.json G:Scope (C2: any real q, tested with q > 0)
steps.if_wrong: A nonuniform q(x) would break the scaling S20 into one with a shape function and change the steady state S44 away from a parabola.

steps.label: A6
steps.statement: T \in C^{2,1}\big((0,L)\times(0,\infty)\big);\quad T,\ \partial_x T,\ \partial_x^2 T,\ \partial_t T \text{ extend continuously to the ends for } t>0, \text{ i.e. } T \in C^{2,1}\big([0,L]\times(0,\infty)\big);\quad T \in C\big([0,L]\times[0,\infty)\big)
steps.source: Regularity hypothesis made here (G:Derivation decision D2(a), strengthened to all of T, T_x, T_xx, T_t up to the ends because S9 and S34 also need T_t there). The interior class serves the localization S12; the class up to the ends for t > 0 serves S9-S11 with a = 0 or b = L, S34, S35, S39; continuity on [0,L] x [0,inf) (including t = 0 and the corners) serves S36 and S48. The boundary and initial data agree in value at the corners (both T_0), so continuity there is compatible with S7. S54 shows the class is not empty: the series solution lies in it.
steps.if_wrong: Without the class up to the ends, the end fluxes S39 are not defined pointwise and the integration by parts in S35 needs a limiting argument. Without continuity at t = 0, S36 cannot conclude E -> 0 as t -> 0+ and uniqueness fails as proved; the minimum principle S48-S50 loses its compact set. The class does not include t = 0 for derivatives: at the corners (0,0), (L,0) the data are incompatible in their derivatives when q != 0 (selection.md item 1), so T_t and T_xx are not continuous there.

steps.label: A7
steps.if_wrong: Other end conditions (flux, Robin) would change S26, S29, S39 and the steady state S44.

steps.label: A8
steps.statement: \text{No grains, ice, vapor or diffuse interface: no } \psi,\ \phi,\ eps,\ eps_s \text{ appear (equivalently } \psi\equiv 1 \text{ and no } \phi)
steps.if_wrong: The toy is not the regolith model; nothing here feeds the PhD model (spec_problem.md lines 110-111).

steps.operation: differentiation under the integral sign (Leibniz rule, fixed limits a, b); needs \partial_t e continuous on [a,b] x (0,inf), which holds by S3 and S6 including a = 0 and b = L
fundamental theorem of calculus (the 1D divergence theorem); needs \partial_x j = -k \partial_x^2 T continuous on [a,b], which holds by S4 and S6 including a = 0 and b = L
substitution of S9 and S10 into S2, then collecting all terms under one integral
steps.statement: \int_a^b \left(\frac{\partial e}{\partial t} + \frac{\partial j}{\partial x} - q\right) dx = 0 \quad \text{for every } 0\le a<b\le L

steps.operation: localization lemma: a continuous function whose integral vanishes over every subinterval vanishes identically. The integrand of S11 is continuous in (0,L) x (0,inf): \partial_t e and \partial_x j are continuous by S6 (through the laws used in S11), and q is continuous because it is constant (S5)
substitution of S3 into S12; \rho and c_p are constant and T_{ref} is constant in t (all three by S1), so \partial_t e = \rho c_p \partial_t T with no -\rho c_p\,dT_{ref}/dt term
steps.statement: \rho c_p \frac{\partial T}{\partial t} + \frac{\partial j}{\partial x} = q

steps.operation: differentiation of S4 in x with the product rule; the term (\partial_x k)(\partial_x T) is zero because k is constant (S1)
substitution of S14 into S13 and moving the conduction term to the right side
steps.statement: \rho c_p \frac{\partial T}{\partial t} = k\,\frac{\partial^2 T}{\partial x^2} + q \quad \text{in } (0,L)\times(0,\infty)

steps.operation: definition of \kappa (notation table, spec_problem.md line 90, approved at G:Scope); well defined and positive because \rho c_p > 0 (S1)
division of S15 by \rho c_p > 0 and substitution of S16
inspection: S15 contains no \psi or \phi, so setting \psi \equiv 1 (grains absent) changes no term
steps.statement: \left.\text{S15}\right|_{\psi\equiv 1} = \text{S15} \quad \text{(the reduction is the identity, term by term: storage, conduction, source)}

steps.label: C1
steps.statement: \text{Reference case: } L=1\,\mathrm{m},\ k=1\,\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}K^{-1}},\ \rho=1\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}},\ c_p=1\,\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}K^{-1}},\ q=1\,\mathrm{W\,m^{-3}},\ T_0=1\,\mathrm{K}
options: (b) a physical material (would need a source)
steps.recommendation: (a): the theta equation has no parameters, so the unit case tests the plumbing fully.
steps.decided: (a), decisions.json G:Scope 2026-11-16T14:17:14-08:00 (approved by the main session for plumbing only), restated at G:Selection and at the G:Derivation send-back note ("C1, C2 and the notation stand for the toy").

steps.operation: definition of the scales (notation table, spec_problem.md lines 93-94, approved at G:Scope); \theta requires \Delta T_q \ne 0, i.e. q \ne 0
steps.statement: \Delta T_q \equiv \frac{qL^2}{k},\quad x_c = L,\quad t_c = \frac{L^2}{\kappa},\quad \xi \equiv \frac{x}{L},\quad \tau \equiv \frac{\kappa t}{L^2},\quad T = T_0 + \Delta T_q\,\theta(\xi,\tau)\quad (q\ne 0)

steps.operation: chain rule in t, with \partial\tau/\partial t = \kappa/L^2 and \partial\xi/\partial t = 0; T is differentiable in t on (0,L) x (0,inf) by S6, so \theta = (T - T_0)/\Delta T_q is differentiable in \tau through the affine map S20

chain rule in x applied twice, with \partial\xi/\partial x = 1/L and \partial\tau/\partial x = 0; T is twice differentiable in x on (0,L) x (0,inf) by S6, so \theta is twice differentiable in \xi through the affine map S20
steps.statement: \frac{\partial T}{\partial x} = \frac{\Delta T_q}{L}\frac{\partial \theta}{\partial \xi},\qquad \frac{\partial^2 T}{\partial x^2} = \frac{\Delta T_q}{L^2}\frac{\partial^2 \theta}{\partial \xi^2}

steps.operation: substitution of S21 and S22 into S17
division of S23 by \kappa\Delta T_q/L^2, which is nonzero because \kappa > 0 (S16), L > 0 and q \ne 0 (S20)
simplification of the coefficient: \rho c_p \kappa = k (S16), then substitution of \Delta T_q = qL^2/k (S20) gives qL^2/(k\cdot qL^2/k) = 1
substitution of S7 into the change of variables S20: x = 0 \mapsto \xi = 0, x = L \mapsto \xi = 1, t = 0 \mapsto \tau = 0, T = T_0 \mapsto \theta = 0
definition of the alternative scaling (spec_problem.md lines 55-57); T_0 > 0 (S7), so it is defined for every q including q = 0
chain rule as in S21-S22 with T_0 in place of \Delta T_q, then substitution into S17
division of S28 by \kappa T_0/L^2 > 0, then \rho c_p\kappa = k (S16); boundary and initial data from S7 divided by T_0
substitution of S20 into S27: Q = (qL^2/k)/T_0 and T_0\theta' = T_0 + \Delta T_q\theta
substitution of the reference values S19(a) into S16, S20, S27 (computed by derivation/scratch/m3_try3.py: kappa = 1, t_c = 1, DeltaT_q = 1, Q = 1)
linearity: subtraction of the equations S17 and data S7 satisfied by two solutions T_1, T_2; q cancels
steps.statement: w \equiv T_1 - T_2:\quad \frac{\partial w}{\partial t} = \kappa\frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial x^2},\quad w(0,t)=w(L,t)=0,\quad w(x,0)=0

steps.operation: multiplication of S33 by w, integration over (0,L), and differentiation under the integral sign (as in S9; w_t is continuous on [0,L] x (0,inf) by S6)
integration by parts on [0,L] (w, w_x, w_xx continuous on [0,L] for t > 0 by S6); the boundary term [w\,\partial_x w]_0^L vanishes because w = 0 at both ends (S33)

(i) continuity at t = 0: w is continuous on the compact set [0,L] x [0,1] (S6), hence uniformly continuous, so max_x |w(x,t)| -> max_x |w(x,0)| = 0 (S33) and E(t) <= (L/2) max_x w^2 -> 0 = E(0) as t -> 0+ (definition of E in S34). (ii) monotonicity: by S35 and the mean value theorem, E(t) <= E(s) for 0 < s < t; letting s -> 0+ gives E(t) <= 0, and E >= 0, so E \equiv 0. (iii) a continuous w with integral of w^2 equal to 0 vanishes identically
steps.statement: T_1 \equiv T_2 \quad \text{(the classical solution of S17 with S7 is unique in the class S6)}

steps.operation: verification by substitution: for q = 0, T \equiv T_0 satisfies S17 and S7 and lies in the class S6, hence is the solution by S36
extreme value theorem: for q \ne 0, \theta = (T - T_0)/\Delta T_q (S20) is continuous on the compact set [0,1] x [0,\tau_1] because T is continuous on [0,L] x [0,inf) (S6), so it attains its minimum

(i) location: \theta = 0 on \xi = 0, \xi = 1 and \tau = 0 (S26), so a negative minimum is attained at 0 < \xi_* < 1, 0 < \tau_* <= \tau_1. (ii) second-derivative test in \xi: \theta(\cdot,\tau_*) is C^2 near the interior point \xi_* (S6 through S20) and has a minimum there, so \partial_\xi\theta = 0 and \partial_\xi^2\theta >= 0. (iii) one-sided difference quotient in \tau: for 0 < h < \tau_*, [\theta(\xi_*,\tau_*) - \theta(\xi_*,\tau_* - h)]/h <= 0 because \theta(\xi_*,\tau_*) is the minimum; \partial_\tau\theta exists at (\xi_*,\tau_*) (S6, \tau_* > 0 is interior to (0,inf)), so letting h -> 0+ gives \partial_\tau\theta <= 0

weak minimum principle by contradiction: if \theta_{min}(\tau_1) < 0, S49 gives \partial_\tau\theta - \partial_\xi^2\theta <= 0 at (\xi_*,\tau_*), but S25 gives \partial_\tau\theta - \partial_\xi^2\theta = 1 > 0 there. So \theta_{min}(\tau_1) >= 0 for every \tau_1 > 0 (S48), and every point of [0,1] x [0,inf) lies in some [0,1] x [0,\tau_1]

(i) uniqueness of \theta: S25-S26 contain no parameter; if \theta_1, \theta_2 both solve S25-S26 in the class S6, the map S20 turns them into two solutions of S17 with S7, which are equal by S36, so \theta_1 = \theta_2 and one \theta serves every q \ne 0. (ii) sign: \Delta T_q = qL^2/k has the sign of q because k > 0 (S1), and \theta >= 0 (S50), so \Delta T_q\theta has the sign of q wherever \theta > 0
steps.statement: \theta(\xi,\tau) \text{ is the same function for every } q\ne 0;\quad T - T_0 = \Delta T_q\,\theta \text{ has the sign of } q \text{ wherever } \theta \ne 0

steps.operation: definition of the outward flux j n with n = -1 at x = 0 and n = +1 at x = L, then substitution of S4; \partial_x T is defined at the ends for t > 0 by S6. Both ends are essential (Dirichlet, S7): no flux condition is imposed and F_0, F_L are outputs
steps.statement: F_0 = -j(0,t) = k\,\frac{\partial T}{\partial x}(0,t),\qquad F_L = j(L,t) = -k\,\frac{\partial T}{\partial x}(L,t)

steps.operation: inspection of S8: there is no solid wall and no phase field, so the contact-angle wall term of Residual_A1 (src/assembly.c lines 81-87) has no counterpart
steady state: setting \partial_\tau\theta = 0 in S25, with the boundary data of S26
integration twice in \xi
matching the boundary conditions of S41: \theta_s(0) = c_0 = 0; \theta_s(1) = -1/2 + c_1 = 0
back-substitution of S20 (T = T_0 + \Delta T_q\theta, \xi = x/L) into S43: (qL^2/k)(x/L)(1-x/L)/2 = qx(L-x)/(2k); for q = 0 the same formula gives T_0, consistent with S37
differentiation of S44, \partial_x T_s = q(L-2x)/(2k), then substitution into S39 at x = 0 and x = L
steps.statement: F_0 = F_L = \frac{qL}{2},\qquad F_0 + F_L = qL = \int_0^L q\,dx

steps.operation: subtraction: \theta_s does not depend on \tau and \theta_s'' = -1 (S41), so \partial_\tau v = -\partial_\tau\theta = -\partial_\xi^2\theta - 1 = -\partial_\xi^2\theta + \theta_s'' = \partial_\xi^2 v by S25; end values 0 - 0 = 0 (S26, S41); initial value \theta_s - 0 (S26, S43)
steps.statement: v \equiv \theta_s - \theta:\quad \frac{\partial v}{\partial \tau} = \frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial \xi^2},\quad v(0,\tau) = v(1,\tau) = 0,\quad v(\xi,0) = \frac{\xi(1-\xi)}{2}

steps.operation: integration by parts, once for the first integral and twice for the second, using \cos(\ell\pi) = (-1)^\ell and \sin(\ell\pi) = \sin 0 = 0; intermediate line: \int_0^1 \xi\cos(\ell\pi\xi)d\xi = ((-1)^\ell - 1)/(\ell\pi)^2
substitution of S43 (2\theta_s = \xi - \xi^2) and subtraction of the two integrals of S52

separation of variables and identification by uniqueness. (i) Each term \beta_\ell\sin(\ell\pi\xi)\exp(-\ell^2\pi^2\tau) solves the equation and end conditions of S51 (sin(\ell\pi\xi) is an eigenfunction of \partial_\xi^2 with eigenvalue -\ell^2\pi^2 and zero end values). (ii) Weierstrass M-test: each term is bounded by \beta_\ell and the sum of \beta_\ell is finite (S53), so the series converges uniformly on [0,1] x [0,inf) and its sum is continuous there; for \tau >= \tau_0 > 0 the differentiated series (\partial_\tau, \partial_\xi, \partial_\xi^2) have terms bounded by a constant times \ell^{-1}\exp(-\ell^2\pi^2\tau_0), which are summable, so term-by-term differentiation is valid and the sum is C^{2,1} on [0,1] x (0,inf). (iii) At \tau = 0 the sum is the sine series of \theta_s, which converges to \theta_s because the odd 2-periodic extension of \theta_s is continuous (\theta_s(0) = \theta_s(1) = 0) and piecewise C^1 (uniform convergence theorem for Fourier series). (iv) So \theta_s minus the series solves S25-S26 in the class S6 (through S20); by the uniqueness in S38 it equals \theta

term-by-term differentiation in \tau for \tau > 0 (justified in S54 (ii)); \partial_\tau\theta = -\partial_\tau v because \theta_s does not depend on \tau (S51); coefficient \ell^2\pi^2 \cdot 4/(\ell\pi)^3 = 4/(\ell\pi)

(i) evaluation at \xi = 1/2, where \sin(\ell\pi/2) = (-1)^r for \ell = 2r+1: the series is alternating with terms a_r = 4/((2r+1)\pi)\exp(-(2r+1)^2\pi^2\tau) that decrease strictly in r and tend to 0, so by the alternating series (Leibniz) bound it is >= a_0 - a_1 = g(\tau). (ii) calculus on g: g'(\tau) = -4\pi\exp(-\pi^2\tau) + 12\pi\exp(-9\pi^2\tau) has one zero, at \tau_g = ln 3/(8\pi^2) = 0.01391, with g' > 0 before and g' < 0 after; so on (0, 0.1], g >= min(g(0+), g(0.1)) = min(8/(3\pi), g(0.1)) = min(0.84883, 0.474487) = 0.474487. Numbers from derivation/scratch/m3_try3.py (run at M3 try 3): \tau_g = 0.0139141; \exp(-0.986960) = 0.372708, times 4/\pi = 1.273240 gives 0.474546; \exp(-8.882644) = 1.38777e-4, times 4/(3\pi) = 0.424413 gives 5.88987e-5; g(0.1) = 0.4744875. g' sampled at \tau_g/2, \tau_g, 2\tau_g, 0.1: +8.59, 0 (to 2e-15), -6.37, -4.68

(i) triangle inequality on S55 with |\sin| <= 1, then factoring \exp(-\pi^2\tau): for \ell = 2r+1 >= 3, \ell^2 - 1 = 4r(r+1) >= 8r and 1/\ell <= 1/3, and the geometric series sum_{r>=1} \exp(-8r\pi^2\tau) = \exp(-8\pi^2\tau)/(1-\exp(-8\pi^2\tau)). (ii) the same on S54 for |v| = |\theta - \theta_s|, with 1/\ell^3 <= 1/27. (iii) both bounds decrease in \tau, so their values at \tau = 1 hold for all \tau >= 1. Numbers at \tau = 1 from derivation/scratch/m3_try3.py (run at M3 try 3): \exp(-\pi^2) = 5.17232e-5; (4/\pi)\exp(-\pi^2) = 6.58560e-5; 4/\pi^3 = 0.129006 and (4/\pi^3)\exp(-\pi^2) = 6.67261e-6; \exp(-8\pi^2) = 5.12e-35, so the bracketed factors are 1 to 34 digits. The scratch series maxima over \xi at \tau = 1 equal these bounds to all printed digits (derivation/scratch/m3_series.py)

comparison of term sizes. Coefficients: all three in S25 equal 1; in S29 they are 1, 1 and Q = 1 for the reference case (S31). Storage: S56 for 0 < \tau <= 0.1 and S57 for \tau >= 1. Conduction: \theta(0,\tau) = 0 for all \tau (S26) and \partial_\tau\theta is continuous up to \xi = 0 (S6), so \partial_\tau\theta(0,\tau) = 0 and S25 gives \partial_\xi^2\theta(0,\tau) = -1 for every \tau > 0. The interval 0.1 < \tau < 1 is a transition in which storage decays like \exp(-\pi^2\tau) (S57)
steps.statement: 0<\tau\le 0.1:\ \max_\xi\partial_\tau\theta \ge 0.47,\ \max_\xi|\partial_\xi^2\theta| \ge 1,\ \text{source} = 1 \ \Rightarrow\ \text{no term is negligible};\quad \tau\ge 1:\ \max_\xi|\partial_\tau\theta| \le 6.6\times 10^{-5},\ \max_\xi|\theta-\theta_s| \le 6.7\times 10^{-6} \ \Rightarrow\ \text{near steady: conduction balances the source}

steps.operation: inspection of S8: the model has no diffuse interface and no eps, so there is no finite-width kinetic error to correct
inspection of S8 and S15: no interface width enters S15, so the limit eps, eps_s \to 0 leaves S15 unchanged and every first-order correction in eps, eps_s is identically zero
